About Us

Advanced science, built for early learners

We believe young children are natural scientists — we just give them the tools, safety, and guidance to go further, sooner. Founded in 2013, Wong Chi Weng's Science College was built around a simple idea: the curiosity kids show at age five doesn't need to wait until high school to be taken seriously.

Our Mission

We give children ages 5 to 9 a genuine head start in science — introducing real lab skills, scientific thinking, and advanced concepts years ahead of the typical curriculum, all through play-based, age-appropriate discovery. Every course is mapped against national primary-science benchmarks, then extended a full grade level beyond them.

  • 🔭 Advanced concepts made simple, never dumbed down.
  • 🧫 Real lab tools, sized and safety-checked for little hands.
  • ❓ Curiosity comes first — every lesson starts with a question.
  • 🏆 Small classes so every child gets real time at the bench.
  • 👩‍🏫 Every instructor holds a science degree plus child-education training.
1

Explore

Every unit opens with a hands-on mystery — a fizzing cup, a shadow that moves, a magnet that "refuses" to touch — before any term is introduced.

2

Experiment

Students run the real procedure themselves at a child-sized lab station, recording results in their own science journal.

3

Explain

Kids present what they found to the class in plain words, building the communication skills that go along with the science.

"I started this college after watching my own daughter lose interest in science by age eight — not because she wasn't curious, but because nothing at school moved at her pace. We built the lab I wish she'd had."

— Wong Chi Weng, Founder
✅ Registered Learning Centre 🧯 Lab Safety Certified 👥 Max 8 Students per Class 🎓 Degree-Qualified Instructors
Courses

Six labs, one curious mind

A full track of advanced science courses, taught progressively as students grow — each one runs as a 12-week term with a hands-on project in the final class.

Chemistry Discovery

Explorer

Kids run real, teacher-supervised reactions using safe, kitchen-grade materials — mixing, measuring, and observing color changes, fizzing, and states of matter, while learning to record results like real chemists do.

👶 Ages 5–9 🗓️ 12-week term ⏱️ 90 min / class 👥 Max 8 students
  • Solids, liquids & gases through hands-on mixing stations
  • Acid-base reactions using cabbage-juice indicators
  • Crystal growing and evaporation over multiple weeks
  • Final project: build a volcano and explain the reaction

Astronomy Explorers

Explorer

From building scale models of the solar system to tracking the moon's phases in a shared class journal, students learn to observe the sky the way astronomers do — patiently, and with real instruments.

👶 Ages 6–9 🗓️ 12-week term 🌙 2 evening telescope nights 👥 Max 8 students
  • The Sun, Earth, and Moon — day, night & the seasons
  • Scale-model solar system build
  • Guided telescope viewing on our rooftop deck
  • Final project: illustrated star map of their own constellation

Robotics Starters

Beginner

Working in pairs, students snap together beginner-friendly robotics kits and program simple behaviors using color-coded blocks — no reading required to start, so even our youngest five-year-olds can build and drive their first robot.

👶 Ages 5–8 🗓️ 12-week term 🤖 Kit provided 👥 Pairs of 2
  • Motors, sensors & wheels — how a robot "feels" its world
  • Block-based programming: loops and if/then logic
  • Maze-solving and obstacle-avoidance challenges
  • Final project: robot demo day for families

Biology & Nature Lab

Explorer

Held partly in our greenhouse classroom, this course has students growing their own plants from seed, examining leaves and insects under real microscopes, and keeping an observation journal across the full term.

👶 Ages 6–9 🗓️ 12-week term 🌱 Take-home plant included 👥 Max 8 students
  • Plant life cycles — germinating and tracking their own seedling
  • Microscope basics: leaves, pollen, and pond water
  • Insects and backyard ecosystems on a nature walk
  • Final project: illustrated field journal to take home

Physics Playground

Intermediate

Physics made physical: students build ramps, pulleys, and levers, then measure speed, force, and balance with real tools — turning abstract ideas like "gravity" and "friction" into things they can push, pull, and time.

👶 Ages 7–9 🗓️ 12-week term ⚙️ Build kits provided 👥 Max 8 students
  • Motion & speed — timing cars down ramps of different angles
  • Pulleys and levers: lifting "heavy" loads with less force
  • Gravity, friction, and air resistance experiments
  • Final project: design a marble run that meets a target time

Coding & Logic

Beginner

Using a colorful block-based coding platform, students build the computational thinking behind every other course — sequencing, loops, and problem-solving — by creating their own mini animations and games.

👶 Ages 6–9 🗓️ 12-week term 💻 Laptop provided in class 👥 Max 8 students
  • Sequencing and loops through block-based coding
  • If/then logic using interactive puzzle challenges
  • Debugging: finding and fixing mistakes in code
  • Final project: build and present a simple animated game
Our Facilities

Six purpose-built labs on one campus

Every course is taught in a dedicated space equipped for that subject — not a shared classroom with supplies wheeled in.

Chemistry Lab

Where Chemistry Discovery meets

  • 8 child-height lab stations with safety trays
  • Kid-safe reagents & color-changing indicators
  • Fume-extraction hood for demonstrations
  • Goggles & aprons sized for ages 5–9
🧯 Fire blanket, eyewash station, and a certified instructor present at all times.

Astronomy Deck

Rooftop viewing space

  • 3 beginner refractor telescopes
  • Retractable roof for clear-sky nights
  • Interactive projector star dome (indoor)
  • Scale solar-system wall model
🌙 Evening sessions always run with two staff present and end-time pickup confirmed with parents.

Robotics Workshop

Build-and-code benches

  • 1 robotics kit per pair of students
  • Tablet stations for block-based programming
  • Obstacle course & maze mats
  • Tool wall sized for small hands
🔧 Kits use low-voltage parts only — no soldering or sharp tools at this age group.

Biology Greenhouse

Living-classroom growing space

  • Personal planting station per student
  • 6 classroom microscopes with prepared slides
  • Butterfly & ladybug observation habitats
  • Outdoor nature-walk trail on campus
🌿 All plants and specimens are non-toxic and allergy-checked before each term.

Physics Yard

Semi-outdoor experiment space

  • Adjustable ramps & marble-run track walls
  • Pulley & lever demonstration rigs
  • Digital stopwatches & force meters
  • Shaded outdoor area for larger builds
🪖 Padded flooring and soft-launch materials — no glass or heavy weights used.

Coding Studio

One laptop per student

  • 8 child-friendly laptops, block-coding software
  • Large shared screen for group demos
  • Printed logic-puzzle worksheets
  • Showcase wall for finished projects
🖥️ Screen time is capped per session and balanced with off-screen logic activities.
